fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The text says the finders brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation (Numbers 15:33). Moses is the one God sent to bring Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10), and Aaron is his brother, whom God set apart to serve as priest (Exodus 28:1). So this went straight to the leaders and the whole congregation, not a quiet word in somebody's ear.

Good guess, friend, because those names do show up in Numbers. Joshua and Caleb are two of the men who explored the land, and they urged Israel not to be afraid (Numbers 14:6, 9). But in this passage, the finders bring the man to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation (Numbers 15:33). No elders are named here. It's a bit like walking into the wrong bakery and asking for the owner.

Eleazar is one of Aaron's sons (Numbers 3:2), so I see why he came to mind. But the text doesn't mention him here at all. The finders brought the man to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation (Numbers 15:33). The tabernacle isn't mentioned in this part of the story either, so I'd keep it out of the picture.

Right on the money, baker. The text says that because it had not been declared what should be done to him, they placed him in custody (Numbers 15:34). He was held while the question was still open. It's the opposite of me eyeballing a recipe, and I've got the burnt batches to prove it.

Sin offerings do come up earlier in this chapter, like the goat in Numbers 15:27, but that's not what the LORD says here. He tells Moses, "The man must surely be put to death." (Numbers 15:35) The answer was given right to Moses, plain and short. It's a heavy moment, so no dancing around it.

Pomegranates do show up on clothing in the Bible, around the hem of a robe for the priest (Exodus 28:33), but they're not what God asks for here. He tells the Israelites to make tassels for the corners of their garments, with a blue cord on each tassel (Numbers 15:38). Keep it simple, friend: corners, tassels, blue cord.

That's it, baker. God says the tassels are "…for you to look at, so that you may remember all the commandments of the LORD…" (Numbers 15:39). One glance down and there's the reminder. It works like a sticky note on the oven door, except mine always ends up covered in flour.

Yes, baker, you caught it. God says the tassels are so they may remember the commandments of the LORD and obey them, "…and not prostitute yourselves by following your own heart and your own eyes." (Numbers 15:39) The tassels point away from following their own heart and eyes, not toward it. It's a tricky one, because the verse names the heart and eyes right there in the middle.

Edom is another real place in the Bible, a land south of the Dead Sea. But it's not the one God names here. He says He is the LORD their God "…who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Numbers 15:41) Egypt is the land He names.
